Sam Liu: Hey people-ops — need to add my stepdaughter to health/dental/vision benefits. We finalized custody yesterday. Is this a qualifying life event for mid-year enrollment? What docs are required and how fast will payroll deductions kick in? cc @Alex (People Ops)

Alex (People Ops): Congrats and thanks for the heads up, Sam. Short answer: yes, custody change usually qualifies as a QLE. You'll have 30 days from the event date to submit via the benefits portal. Docs we need: birth certificate for the child, court/custody order showing legal custody, and a signed enrollment form.

Sam Liu: Thanks — do scanned PDFs work? I have the court order as a PDF.

Alex (People Ops): Scanned PDFs are fine. File names helpful: `birth_certificate_sam_stepdaughter.pdf`, `custody_order.pdf`. Upload under "Report a Qualifying Event" in the portal. I'll paste steps below.

Alex (People Ops): Steps:
1) Sign into benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.com (or open the SSO link in the HR page)
2) Choose "Report a Qualifying Event" -> "Add dependent (custody/legal guardianship)"
3) Fill effective date = custody date (yesterday)
4) Upload the two docs and hit Submit
5) Confirm with us via DM if you want us to review the submission

Maria Ortega: Quick Q — does this change affect Sam's HSA elections? If dependent is added, HSA contribution limits may change if switching to family coverage.

Alex (People Ops): Good call. If you add the dependent to the medical plan and it moves you from individual to family coverage, your HSA contribution limits increase. Payroll will pro-rate deductions going forward from the effective date; retro pay for premiums is not typical, but carriers often handle eligibility retroactively if the QLE is filed within 30 days.

Sam Liu: How long until coverage is active once I submit? I need to know for an upcoming dentist appointment.

Alex (People Ops): Medical/dental/vision coverage effective date = the custody date you enter. Claims should be covered once the carrier processes the addition — carriers usually update within 7–10 business days after submission. For urgent appts, keep the claim explanation and we can do a benefits escalation (we've done a few in similar situations).

BenefitsBot: Reminder — people-ops office hours today 2–4pm PST. Portal FAQ: https://benefits.redwood.com/faq

Sam Liu: Perfect, submitting now. Thanks!

Alex (People Ops): I see your portal submission (ticket #B-2025-884). I'll review docs and follow up if the carrier needs anything else. :thumbsup:

Sam Liu: Got it, thanks Alex.
